Bean & Leaf, a locally owned coffee shop, opened its doors on Maple Street last Friday, drawing long lines of customers eager to try its signature roasts. Owner Diane Cho, who previously worked as a barista in Seattle for over a decade, says she wanted to bring specialty coffee to her hometown.

The shop sources its beans directly from small farms in Colombia and Ethiopia, and all pastries are baked fresh daily on-site. In addition to coffee, Bean & Leaf offers a small selection of teas and light snacks.

Cho plans to introduce a loyalty program next month, offering regular customers discounts and free drinks after a certain number of purchases.

choices: A loyalty program will be introduced

Effective next month, employees will be permitted to work from home up to two days per week, subject to manager approval. This new policy is designed to offer greater flexibility while maintaining team collaboration and productivity.

Employees wishing to participate should discuss their preferred remote days with their manager and confirm the arrangement in writing. Core hours of 10 AM to 3 PM must still be observed, during which employees should be available for meetings and calls regardless of their location.

We will review the effectiveness of this policy after six months and make adjustments as needed.

The city council approved plans last week to add 15 miles of new bicycle lanes throughout the downtown area, aiming to reduce traffic congestion and promote environmentally friendly transportation. Construction is expected to begin in early spring and finish before the summer tourist season.

Local cycling groups have praised the decision, noting that the current lanes are often disconnected and unsafe. However, some downtown business owners have expressed concern about the temporary loss of parking spaces during construction.

City officials say they will work closely with businesses to minimize disruption and have promised additional parking studies once the project is complete.

GreenLeaf Appliances is voluntarily recalling its Model X200 electric kettle due to a potential electrical malfunction that could pose a fire hazard. Approximately 12,000 units sold between January and April of this year are affected.

Customers who own an affected model should stop using it immediately and contact GreenLeaf's customer service line for a free replacement or full refund. The model number can be found on a label on the bottom of the kettle.

GreenLeaf apologizes for any inconvenience this may cause and emphasizes that customer safety remains its top priority.
